title: Lipschitz stability of Gaussian extensions
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then the difference between the expectations of $\psi$ applied to the two multilinear extensions of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$, under the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, satisfies
\[
\left|\int_{\mathbb R^n}\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}z_i\right)d\gamma^{\otimes n}(z)-\int_{\mathbb R^n}\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat g(S)\prod_{i\in S}z_i\right)d\gamma^{\otimes n}(z)\right|\le c\,\|f-g\|_2,
\]
where $\widehat f(S)=\E[f\chi_S]$ and $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, and the norm is for uniform measure on the Boolean cube.
hypotheses_covered: A function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ that is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$
